title: NOT EXISTS
story: Find the products that nobody has ordered.
goal: Show the name of products with no orders at all, alphabetically (column name).
starter:
SELECT name FROM products p
WHERE ;

tests.label: Finds products with no orders (NOT EXISTS, NOT IN or LEFT JOIN)
Hidden check on other data

hints: NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE ...) is true when the inner query finds nothing.
Connect the inner query to the outer row: o.product_id = p.id.
SELECT name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.product_id = p.id) ORDER BY name;
socratic: What does the inner query look at for each product?
Which other way finds the same rows?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the Finds products with no orders (NOT EXISTS, NOT IN or LEFT JOIN)?
solution: SELECT name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.product_id = p.id) ORDER BY name;
alt: SELECT p.name FROM products p LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.product_id = p.id WHERE o.id IS NULL ORDER BY p.name;
